questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Ecuador?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Ecuador article.

questions.proof: The capital of the country is Quito.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Ecuador?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Ecuador on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Ecuador article.

questions.proof: Peru borders Ecuador to the south, and Colombia borders it to the north.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Ecuador?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Population” part of the Ecuador article.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Ecuador?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Ecuador article.

questions.proof: Since then, the country uses the United States dollar for money, but its coins (not the banknotes) are different from those in the US.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ was interested in finding gold in Ecuador.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “interested”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ecuador article.

questions.proof: Spain was interested in finding gold in Ecuador.
